sources.entry: md-preview - Ultra-lightweight Markdown preview app (~1MB binary) built with Rust, with offline syntax highlighting, dark mode, and cross-platform support.

summary.one_liner: MD Preview is a Rust-based, local-first Markdown previewer and quick editor that uses the system WebView, with tabs, autosave, offline math and Mermaid rendering, and native mobile shells for iOS and Android.
summary.what_it_does: MD Preview opens one or more local .md and .txt files in a single tabbed window on desktop, restoring tab order and the active document after restart. It renders Markdown with GFM tables, task lists, strikethrough, GitHub-style alerts, ==highlight== marks, and YAML front matter, with syntax highlighting, KaTeX math and Mermaid diagrams loaded locally. Relative and absolute links to local Markdown or text files open or activate tabs, and relative images resolve from the file's directory. It includes a simple source editor with debounced autosave, live reload when another editor changes the file, in-preview find, content zoom from 70% to 200%, and print of only the preview. The README also describes native iOS and Android shells for opening Markdown from Files and share sheets, and a macOS Finder extension for creating new Markdown files.
use_cases: preview README or plan files generated by AI coding tools
read local documentation folders with linked files
quick edits to a Markdown file without opening an IDE
export a clean PDF from Markdown via print
view Markdown and text files on Android or iOS from Files or share sheets
create a new Markdown note from Finder on macOS
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL> (the README leaves the URL blank)
notable: Uses the system WebView (WebKit, WebView2, WebKitGTK) instead of bundling Chromium or Electron, with a release binary around 1MB
Tabbed desktop window where local document links open or activate tabs
Autosave with flush on tab switch, close, or quit, and preserved content when saves fail
Fully offline rendering of syntax highlighting, math and diagrams, with heavy enhancers deferred until needed
Windows self-updater verifies SHA-256 before replacing the exe; no telemetry or accounts
caveats: Apple platform downloads, package builds and signing are suspended; macOS/iOS features refer to retained source code only
Linux requires the system WebKitGTK runtime (4.1), and NVIDIA systems may need workarounds for a blank window
Android is released separately from desktop builds
Windows cannot be set as default app automatically; the user must choose it from Open with
